During operation, a staff of 290 production personnel will be required to produce 15 million tons per year on Tract III. Mining of 4 million tons per year for export from Tract II during years 1982 through 2070 would require approximately 100 production personnel. These will include management personnel, foremen, equipment operators and laborers. This will allow for three shifts for a portion of the operating personnel. Chapter III has more detailed information of payroll and workers for this rate of development.
High Level Development
The maximum level of development involves the removal and shipment of 26 million tons of coal annually by 1992. This level of coal extraction requires 2 draglines upon Tract II for 8 million tons annual production and 4 draglines upon Tract III for 18 million tons annual production as shown on Table I-2.
Westmoreland Resources, in helping develop projections for a maximum development scenario, has indicated that Tract III production of coal for shipment could reach 18 million tons annually by 1992 at the earliest. Coal production at this rate would remain constant until the coal reserves of 850 million tons are exhausted in 2030. Under the maximum level of coal production 8 million tons of coal would be mined and exported annually by 1990 from Tract II. This rate of production would continue until the coal reserves of 350 million tons are exhausted in approximately 2030.
